body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in **agent self-improvement route** that lets Sepo propose and apply improvements to itself.

- **`agent-self-improvement.yml`** — opt-in scheduled/manual planner workflow
- **`agent-self-improvement` prompt** — planner guidance
- **Deterministic decision application** — `apply-self-improvement-decision` CLI applies an approved self-improvement decision reproducibly
- **Requester resolution** — `resolve-self-improvement-requester` CLI + `self-improvement-requester.ts` scope who may request or trust a proposal
- **Core route** — `self-improvement.ts` (markers, trace comments, and orchestrator dispatch wiring)
- **Docs + regression coverage** — configuration list, supported-workflows docs, and unit tests

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 764b77ac7b784a191a594e7b5e6a03edd90cf3a1 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
This PR adds an opt-in `agent-self-improvement` workflow that lets Sepo periodically or manually plan a self-improvement step. The design separates a read-only planner decision from a deterministic apply job that creates or comments on a target and dispatches `agent-orchestrator.yml`. It also adds requester resolution, decision parsing/application logic, docs, and focused tests. The main goal is to make self-improvement liveness possible while keeping writes in reviewed CLI code.

## Review
The overall design is strong, but one authorization sequencing issue remains blocking: the apply step can create a Sepo-authored issue or comment before validating that the requester may use the delegated initial orchestrate capability set. Reviewer outputs disagreed on severity, but the current PR code supports treating this as blocking.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Apply writes before delegated access validation | BLOCKING | `.agent/src/cli/apply-self-improvement-decision.ts` creates a proposal issue or posts a continuation comment before the initial orchestrate access-policy check runs. Downstream preflight can stop orchestration, but only after the side effect exists. |
| Shared orchestration helpers are duplicated | WARNING | The apply CLI rebuilds the orchestrator dispatch envelope, and requester resolution duplicates association precedence already handled by existing helpers. This is a drift risk rather than an immediate behavior break. |
| Self-improvement proposal prompt should harden untrusted context handling | WARNING | The planner inspects issues, PRs, and repo context, then writes `new_issue` title/body content into a Sepo-authored issue. The prompt/docs should explicitly frame external issue/PR text as data, not instructions. |
| Configuration row is dense | INFO | The `AGENT_SELF_IMPROVEMENT_ENABLED` configuration-list entry is accurate but packs setup guidance and implementation caveats into one table cell. This is already documented more fully elsewhere. |

## Progress
- Existing inline comments and review threads were fetched before mutation; none existed.
- Posted one inline comment on `.agent/src/cli/apply-self-improvement-decision.ts:323` for the blocking side-effect-before-access-check issue.
- No inline comments were minimized, replied to, or resolved.
- Rubrics review already noted the dense configuration row as non-blocking and reported focused build/tests passing.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Apply writes before delegated access validation</summary>

**Cause:** The apply CLI calls `createNewProposalIssue()` for `new_issue` and `postContinuationComment()` for continuations before `dispatchOrchestrator()` forwards `AUTHOR_ASSOCIATION` and `ACCESS_POLICY` to the orchestrator. The actual initial-orchestrate delegated capability check currently lives downstream in `initialOrchestrateCapabilityStopReason()` via orchestrator preflight.

**Candidate solutions:** Run the same initial orchestrate capability validation inside the apply CLI before any create/comment side effect, reusing `initialOrchestrateCapabilityStopReason()` or extracting a shared helper. Add a regression test where a denied requester plus restrictive `AGENT_ACCESS_POLICY` exits before issue creation, comments, or dispatch.

**Comments:** Codex flagged this as blocking; the rubrics and Claude reviews considered delegated authorization preserved because the downstream orchestrator rechecks it. The current code confirms the downstream check is too late to prevent the Sepo-authored issue/comment side effect.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Shared orchestration helpers are duplicated</summary>

**Cause:** `dispatchOrchestrator()` reconstructs the `agent-orchestrator.yml` input envelope already built by `dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts`, and `resolveSelfImprovementRequester()` reimplements association precedence instead of delegating to `resolveGithubActorAssociation()`.

**Candidate solutions:** Extract a shared orchestrator dispatch input builder and reuse the canonical actor association resolver for the manual-dispatch branch, keeping only the self-improvement-specific schedule handling and output labels local.

**Comments:** This is useful cleanup but not required to unblock the PR if the authorization sequencing fix stays focused.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Self-improvement proposal prompt should harden untrusted context handling</summary>

**Cause:** The planner can inspect untrusted issue/PR text and then place derived content into a Sepo-authored proposal issue that the orchestrator later processes with elevated requester context.

**Candidate solutions:** Update the planner prompt to explicitly treat external issue/PR text as untrusted data rather than instructions, and add a short operator-facing note in the self-improvement docs about this trust boundary.

**Comments:** This is bounded by the normal PR review/merge gates, so it is not the blocking item.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Configuration row is dense</summary>

**Cause:** The `AGENT_SELF_IMPROVEMENT_ENABLED` row includes operational behavior, marker/dedupe details, and authorship caveats in one compact configuration table entry.

**Candidate solutions:** Keep the table row to the enablement summary and move deeper runtime caveats to the supported-workflows documentation.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The blocking issue is a concrete branch change that can be fixed deterministically by validating delegated route access before any apply-step issue/comment side effects.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Validate initial orchestrate delegated-route access in the self-improvement apply CLI before creating proposal issues, posting continuation comments, or dispatching the orchestrator.
- [ ] Add a regression test proving a denied requester plus restrictive `AGENT_ACCESS_POLICY` produces no issue, comment, or dispatch side effects.
